data.title: Russia's plague scare: What we know
data.description: MOSCOW - The death of a plague laboratory worker in Siberia last week has made global headlines, with Russian media suggesting hundreds were under quarantine and US President Donald Trump expressing concern.

data.title: Russia warns of 'false' information as second plague case reported
data.description: MOSCOW - Russia warned Wednesday against "false" information as reports emerged of a second suspected case of plague in Siberia, with Washington and Brussels calling for transparency and neighbouring Mongolia tightening health surveillance.

data.title: Thousands march fearing return of a Bolsonaro presidency in Brazil
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - Thousands of people joined a student march Wednesday in downtown Rio de Janeiro to protest presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and a surge of the far-right in Brazil.

data.title: Trump says 'we don't think' Russian plague is bio-weapon
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Wednesday that the death of a Russian plague laboratory worker did not appear to be linked to a biological weapon.

data.title: WHO says cannot conduct full risk assessment on Russia plague reports
data.description: GENEVA - The World Health Organization said Wednesday it could not produce a full risk assessment as it did not have the whole picture from Russia on the suspected plague death of a laboratory technician.

data.title: German Chancellor marks October 7 with vow to fight antisemitism
data.description: BERLIN - Chancellor Friedrich Merz marked the third anniversary of the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel by vowing to fight antisemitism in Germany while pressing for a two-state solution in the Israel-Palestinian conflict.

data.title: Spared, married, hanged: an Iranian protester’s last weeks
data.description: Alireza Sepahi was arrested in the wake of Iran’s January protests, was spared public execution in July after suffering a heart attack and married his fiancee on the eve of his death.

data.title: German ex-spy chief kept in jail after treason arrest
data.description: BERLIN - A court Wednesday ordered former German spy chief August Hanning to remain in jail after his arrest on suspicion of espionage and treason, along with a former deputy who allegedly supplied him with secret files.

data.title: Heavy casualties in Ukraine after Russian strikes
data.description: PRYLUKY, Ukraine - At least 20 people were killed in Russian strikes across Ukraine on Wednesday, including 14 when a missile slammed into an apartment block in the north of the country as they slept.

data.title: French-Japanese duo win Nobel chemistry prize
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Henri Kagan of France and Kenso Soai of Japan have been awarded the Nobel chemistry prize for solving the mystery of why only one version of some molecules’ mirror-image forms appears in nature, a discovery decisive for the development of pharmaceuticals.

data.title: Russia glosses over dark Soviet past in reinvented museum
data.description: MOSCOW - In a Moscow museum that once housed evidence of Stalin-era repression, serene family scenes flickered on a screen as a narrator hailed the tranquility of pre-World War II life in the Soviet Union.

data.title: Nasa rover takes striking image of dawn's early light on Mars
data.description: WASHINGTON — The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (Nasa) has released a striking image of dawn ‌on the Martian surface taken by its Curiosity rover, showing sunlight bathing jagged crags formed billions of years ago as the car-sized vehicle continues to explore Earth's planetary neighbour.

data.title: Mayor of opposition stronghold Izmir defects to Erdogan party
data.description: ANKARA - The mayor of Izmir, Turkey's third city and an opposition stronghold, on Wednesday defected to the ruling AKP, in a huge symbolic victory for Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

data.title: Rubio in Greece to warn against ‘decline’ of Western civilisation
data.description: ATHENS - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Athens on Wednesday ahead of a “strategic dialogue” with the NATO member on regional and energy security, the State Department said.

data.title: Yemen's Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi airports
data.description: RIYADH - The Houthis claimed a flurry of attacks on Saudi targets on Wednesday including firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh airport, as the group battles for territory in Yemen against government forces supported by the kingdom.

data.title: France suspends stun grenade use at student protests
data.description: PARIS - France has suspended the use of stun grenades by police at student-led demonstrations, the interior minister said Wednesday, as allegations of police brutality mounted after days of sometimes violent demonstrations across the country.

data.title: Micron workers at Taiwan plant vote in favour of strike
data.description: TAIPEI - Hundreds of workers at a Micron Technology plant in Taiwan have voted to strike, their union said Wednesday, after talks with the US memory chip giant over bonus reforms collapsed.

data.title: Myanmar leader lands in Malaysia for migrant return talks
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Myanmar's leader landed for his first visit to Malaysia on Wednesday, since taking power in a 2021 coup, as Kuala Lumpur seeks his cooperation to return thousands of migrants.

data.title: US military face curfew, alcohol ban on Okinawa after murder case
data.description: TOKYO - US forces on Okinawa were on Wednesday barred from drinking alcohol for 48 hours and also face a 30-day curfew after the murder of a woman allegedly committed by an American Marine.

data.title: Mourning, war and elections as Israel marks Oct 7
data.description: RE'IM — Israel marked the third anniversary of Hamas's attack on Oct 7 on Wednesday with silent tributes, new strikes on Gaza and intense political debate, weeks before elections in which the country's deadliest day will be front and centre.

data.title: Malaysia’s Myanmar bet? Repatriations pave way for diplomacy
data.description: BEIJING — Malaysia’s repatriation of Myanmar nationals ahead of a visit to Kuala Lumpur by the war-torn country’s leader appears to mirror efforts by other Southeast Asian countries seeking to mend ties with Nay Pyi Taw.
